bib.title: MoE-LLaVA: Mixture of Experts for Large Vision-Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: MoE-LLaVA: Mixture of Experts for Large Vision-Language Models. Bin Lin, Zhenyu Tang, Yang Ye, Jinfa Huang, Junwu Zhang, Yatian Pang, Peng Jin, Munan Ning, Jiebo Luo, Li Yuan. arXiv:2401.15947v5 (23 Dec 2024), ICML-style template. The extraction names no venue, so treat it as preprint. Year 2024.

COVERAGE: 22 of 22 pages read. 92,184 chars read, with the main text in full and the appendix at pages 15-19 (A.1, A.2, B.1-B.5). The reference list (about 400 lines) was skimmed only. Routing-figure axis labels (Figs 7-14) are plot text only. Table 12 chat examples were read.

CLAIMS
(ranked)
- claim: Converting an LLM to an LVLM and sparsifying it in one stage degrades performance. A three-stage MoE-Tuning recipe avoids this. Stage I trains only the MLP projector. Stage II trains the full LLM as a dense LVLM. Stage III copies the FFN into each expert and trains only the MoE/FFN layers.
  number: none
  setup: CLIP-Large/336 encoder, 2-layer MLP projector, LLaVA-1.5 style. Small LLM backbones.
  quote: "We observe that simultaneously converting LLM to LVLM and sparsifying the model leads to significant performance degradation. After multiple attempts, we find that proper initialization is crucial for sparsifying the LVLM"
  where: p2, intro
- claim: Training-strategy ablation. Direct MoE training (a) is worst. Dense LVLM stage II on Hybrid-FT followed by MoE stage III (b) is best on GQA, SQA and POPE.
  number: (a) GQA 58.4, SQA-I 58.1, POPE 81.9, LLaVA-W 88.0. (b) 61.5, 63.1, 87.0, 88.7. (c) 60.9, 60.2, 86.4, 86.3. (d) 60.9, 62.5, 86.9, 90.1
  setup: Qwen-1.8B x4 Top2 (it is the setting highlighted in the Table 5 caption). Table 6. Variant (d) has no MoE in stage III, so it is a dense control.
  quote: "(a) ✔ - LV+Hb 58.4 58.1 81.9 88.0 (b) ✔ Hb LV 61.5 63.1 87.0 88.7"
  where: Table 6, p8
- claim: With about 3B activated parameters the model approaches LLaVA-1.5-7B on understanding benchmarks. It beats LLaVA-1.5-13B on POPE hallucination.
  number: MoE-LLaVA-2.7Bx4-Top2: 3.6B activated, 5.3B total. SQA-I 68.5 vs 66.8, MMB 65.2 vs 64.3, LLaVA-W 94.1 vs 63.4, MM-Vet 34.3 vs 30.5. VQAv2 77.6 vs 78.5. POPE 86.3 vs 85.9. MME 1423.0 vs 1510.7 (LLaVA-1.5-7B)
  setup: 336 res, zero-shot. VQAv2 and GQA carry an asterisk for training-data overlap. Table 3.
  quote: "MoE-LLaVA-2.7B×4-Top2 P-2.7B 3.6B 336 77.6∗ 61.4∗ 43.9 68.5 51.4 86.3 1423.0 65.2 94.1 34.3"
  where: Table 3, p6
- claim: The intro quotes gains over LLaVA-1.5-7B for the 3.6B-activated model. Check this against Table 3. The 30.7% LLaVA-W figure matches the table's 94.1 vs 63.4. The VQAv2 and MME columns are slightly below the 7B model.
  number: 1.9%, 0.4%, 0.9%, 30.7%, 3.8% (ScienceQA, POPE, MMBench, LLaVAW, MM-Vet)
  setup: 3.6B activated
  quote: "which outperform LLaVA-1.5-7B by 1.9%, 0.4%, 0.9%, 30.7%, and 3.8% in ScienceQA, POPE, MMBench, LLaVAW, and MM-Vet, respectively"
  where: p2
  note: The text elsewhere says "surpasses LLaVA-1.5-7B by 2.7% on SQAI" (p5). Table 3 gives 68.5 vs 66.8, a 1.7 point gap. The text and table do not agree. Cite the table.
- claim: POPE object hallucination. The 2.2B-activated model beats LLaVA-1.5-13B on all three subsets.
  number: MoE-LLaVA-1.8Bx4 Acc 86.1 / 88.6 / 88.7 (Adversarial/Popular/Random) vs LLaVA-1.5-13B 85.5 / 87.4 / 88.0. Gains of 1.0%, 1.5%, 0.8% in the text. Yes-ratio 44.9 / 42.5 / 43.0
  setup: Table 4, zero-shot POPE.
  quote: "MoE-LLaVA-1.8B×4 surpasses LLaVA-1.5-13B by 1.0%, 1.5%, and 0.8% in adversarial sampling, popular sampling, and random sampling, respectively, with 2.2B activated parameters."
  where: Sec 4.3, p6
- claim: The 2.7B-activated-class MoE beats its dense Phi-2 base after the full recipe. Gains are larger on LLaVA-W and VQAv2.
  number: Phi-2 dense vs MoE: VQAv2 75.6 -> 77.6, SQA-I 67.8 -> 68.5, TextVQA 50.0 -> 51.4, MMB 65.0 -> 65.2, LLaVA-W 91.3 -> 94.1. StableLM: VQAv2 74.5 -> 76.7 (Table 7) or 76.0 (Table 10)
  setup: Tables 7 and 10. The dense baselines are trained with the same recipe, per the paper's framing.
  quote: "Phi-2 ✗ 75.6 67.8 50.0 65.0 91.3✔ 77.6 68.5 51.4 65.2 94.1"
  where: Table 7 p8
- claim: Scaling to 7B did not work. The OpenChat-7B MoE is worse than its dense base on SQA-I, TextVQA, MMB and LLaVA-W. The authors blame insufficient multimodal tuning data.
  number: OpenChat dense vs MoE: VQAv2 77.9 -> 78.9, SQA-I 69.0 -> 62.8, TextVQA 54.7 -> 52.5, MMB 66.9 -> 65.9, LLaVA-W 89.7 -> 86.3. OpenChat 7B Top2 has 9.6B activated, 15.2B total
  setup: Table 10, 8 in Table 8.
  quote: "the overall performance of OpenChat-MoE is significantly inferior to dense models. We speculate that this may be due to the insufficient data for current multi-modal instruction tuning to support sparse pattern learning in 10B-level models"
  where: App B.1, p16
- claim: Tuning only the FFN/MoE layers matches full-parameter tuning in stage III at about 75% of the time.
  number: FFN: GQA 61.5, VisWiz 32.6, TextVQA 48.0, POPE 87.0, LLaVA-W 88.7, 20h. All: 61.3, 31.9, 47.6, 87.0, 88.1, 27h
  setup: 8 V100-32G, Qwen-1.8B x4 Top2. Table 5a.
  quote: "tuning the FFN is sufficient to achieve results comparable to full-parameter tuning, but it requires only approximately 75% of the time"
  where: Sec 4.5, p8
- claim: More experts and top-2 beat top-1. Placing MoE in alternating layers beats all-layers MoE, which is slower and no better.
  number: 1 expert vs 2 experts (Table 5b): POPE 86.4 -> 87.5, SQA-I 60.2 -> 60.8. Top-1 vs Top-2: VQAv2 74.5 -> 76.2, POPE 85.7 -> 88.7, 19h -> 20h. Architecture: Interval POPE 88.7 at 20h vs All 87.0 at 32h
  setup: Table 5b-5d. The table lists 1 or 2 experts, not 4.
  quote: "using "All" does not yield better results and results in longer training times compared to other architectures. Therefore, MoE-LLaVA alternates the insertion of MoE layers."
  where: Sec 4.5, p8
- claim: Higher expert capacity (1.5 vs 1.0, Batch Priority Routing) improves results consistently.
  number: avg 60.6 vs 59.9 (1.6Bx4), 64.7 vs 63.9 (2.7Bx4 at 336), 66.7 vs 65.8 (2.7Bx4 at 384)
  setup: Table 11. The averages are over the ten benchmarks in the table.
  quote: "Increasing the capacity consistently improves performance for different sizes of MoE-LLaVA."
  where: App B.2, p16
- claim: Routing analysis. Expert loads are balanced overall. Specific experts dominate specific depth ranges. Text and image tokens have similar routing, so no modality-specific experts emerge.
  number: none. Phi-2 model: expert 3 dominates layers 17-27 on ScienceQA. Appendix quotes 17-23 for Fig 8
  setup: MoE-LLaVA-2.7Bx4-Top2 on ScienceQA (Fig 4-6). The 7B OpenChat model has a flatter, more balanced routing.
  quote: "Each expert in MoE-LLaVA is capable of handling both text tokens and image tokens simultaneously, which demonstrates that MoE-LLaVA does not exhibit a clear preference for any modality."
  where: Sec 4.4, p6-7
- claim: Higher input resolution (384) lifts the 2.7Bx4 model. The model also beats Qwen-VL-7B on MMBench and IDEFICS-80B.
  number: 384 res: VQAv2 79.9, SQA-I 70.3, TextVQA 57.0, MMB 68.0, LLaVA-W 97.3, MM-Vet 35.9. Text says +21.5% over Qwen-VL-7B on MMBench
  setup: Table 3.
  quote: "MoE-LLaVA-Qwen-1.8B×4 surpasses Qwen-VL-7B by 21.5%, on MMBench, despite the latter utilizing higher image resolutions."
  where: p6

ARCHITECTURE FACTS (Table 1 / A.1)
- Router is a linear layer W in R^(D x E) with softmax. Top-k=2 of E=4 experts. Output is the softmax-weighted sum of the top-k expert outputs.
- MoE replaces every other FFN (half the layers).
- Total loss = autoregressive loss + alpha * load-balancing loss (Fedus et al. 2022). alpha = 0.01.
- Activated/total params: StableLM-1.6Bx4 2.0B/2.9B. Qwen-1.8Bx4 2.2B/3.1B. Phi2-2.7Bx4 3.6B/5.3B.

TRAINING SETUP (Tables 2, 9)
- Stage I: LLaVA-PT 558k. Stage II: Hybrid-FT 964k (SViT-157k, LVIS-220k, LRV-331k, MIMIC-IT-256k). Stage III: LLaVA-mix-665k.
- LRs: 1e-3 / 2e-5 / 2e-5. 1 epoch ("the models overfit when training for 2 epochs").
- Bf16. 8xA800-80G. Ablation timings on 8xV100-32G. DeepSpeed Zero2 (Zero2 offload for stage 3, since Zero3 does not support MoE).

LIMITS
- Authors concede: "we observe some difficulties in training stability, particularly with 16-bit float precision" (p9). Appendix A.2: fp16 sometimes gives NaN loss.
- 7B-scale MoE underperforms dense (see claim above). The authors' explanation, insufficient data, is speculation, not tested.
- The headline "comparable to 7B" holds on ScienceQA, POPE, MMBench, LLaVA-W, MM-Vet. It is below on MME (1423 vs 1511), VQAv2 (77.6 vs 78.5) and GQA (61.4 vs 62.0). Several VQAv2/GQA numbers carry a training-data-overlap asterisk.
- LLaVA-W and MM-Vet are GPT-judged open-ended benchmarks. The +30.7% LLaVA-W gap is partly caused by the 7B baseline's low score of 63.4 (in this table).
- Activated parameters are counted, not measured latency or memory. Total parameters are 1.5x or more the activated count, so memory is not saved. No throughput or serving numbers are given.
- Table 12 shows failure cases. The model names "Elon Musk" or "Leonardo da Vinci" for photos or paintings, apparently wrong or unchecked. Not analyzed as a limitation.
- Dated: 2024 small backbones (StableLM, Qwen-1.8B, Phi-2), CLIP-L/336, LLaVA-1.5 data. Later LVLMs are not compared.
- Text and tables disagree in places (SQA-I +2.7% vs table 1.7; StableLM MoE VQAv2 76.7 in Table 7 vs 76.0 in Table 10).

BUILDS ON
- LLaVA 1.5 (Liu et al., 2023b/c): architecture, data and eval protocol. CLIP-Large (Radford et al., 2021) as vision encoder.
- MoE: Jacobs et al., 1991. Eigen et al., 2013. Shazeer et al., 2017. Lepikhin et al., 2020 (GShard). Fedus et al., 2022 (Switch, load-balancing loss). Zoph et al., 2022. Komatsuzaki et al., 2022 (sparse upcycling, the FFN-copy init). Mixtral (Jiang et al., 2024).
- Multimodal MoE: LIMoE (Mustafa et al., 2022), EVE (Chen et al., 2023a), MoCLE (Gou et al., 2023, the closest work).
- Batch Priority Routing (Riquelme et al., 2021).
- POPE (Li et al., 2023d) for hallucination.

CODE: none (the repo is linked at https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/MoE-LLaVA). Load-bearing formulas:
- "P(x)i = e^f(x)i / sum_j e^f(x)j" (Eq 5, p4), "MoE(x) = sum_{i=1..k} P(x)i · E(x)i" (Eq 6), "Ltotal = Lregressive + α·Laux" (Eq 7), "Laux = E · sum Fi·Gi" (Eq 9).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p1): average POPE vs activated parameters across open LVLMs. MoE-LLaVA-1.8Bx4 sits above the linear fit. Shows the hallucination claim at a glance.
- Fig 2 (p2) and Fig 3 (p3): the three-stage MoE-Tuning, showing which parts are frozen or trained at each stage and the FFN copy to experts. This is the clearest picture of the method.
- Fig 4-5 (p7): expert load and modality distribution per layer on ScienceQA. Fig 6: top-10 token pathways. Appendix Figs 7-14 repeat these for OpenChat, Phi, Qwen and StableLM.

PROBLEMS: Extraction is clean apart from garbled ligatures ("LLaV A"). Figure and table text from the plots is interleaved. No embedded instructions found. Table 3 column alignment is flattened but readable. Table 5 and Table 11 row pairings were inferred from adjacent values. Table 11 in particular has merged "1.5"/"1.0" rows.
